content:
Facts: Son appointed sole heir by mother's public will except sibling's legitimate portion; will acknowledged €150,000 debt to appointed heir for renovation work, stipulating debt borne entirely by legitimate heir; will stated legitimate heir owed €10,400 loan balance; appointed heir sued for payment; legitimate heir counterclaimed challenging testamentary debt allocation, asserting mother owed him compensation for property non-enjoyment, claiming maintenance contract nullity (alternatively simulation concealing donation infringing legitimate portion), challenging destination restriction validity, requesting Clio car inclusion in estate.
Legal Framework: Articles 540, 549, 724-725, 752, 979, 1817, 2645-ter Italian Civil Code (spousal habitation right; encumbrances on legitimate portion; debt attribution to heir's share; inheritance costs; usufruct extinction; loan repayment deadline; destination acts); maintenance contract case law (Cass. SU 6532/1994, Cass. 14796/2009, Cass. 2283/1980).
Interpretive Issues: Whether testamentary provision charging entire deceased's debt to legitimate heir violates Art. 549 prohibition on encumbrances; limitation period calculation for loan lacking repayment deadline; whether co-heir's debt to deceased payable directly to requesting co-heir or attributable to debtor's estate share; legitimacy of compensation claims for property non-enjoyment when deceased held habitation right; maintenance contract validity requiring alea element; evidentiary standard for contract simulation concealing donation; destination act validity absent ownership transfer; legitimacy of unilateral self-destination; vehicle ownership determination when third party paid purchase price.
Principles Applied: Article 549 prohibition interpreted broadly protecting legitimate portion's quantitative integrity; Art. 713-768 exception covers only limitations applicable to legitimate heirs (timing restrictions, share formation, valuation designation, division procedures), not provisions nullifying quantitative protection. Testamentary stipulation charging deceased's debt entirely to legitimate heir ineffective; debt divided pro rata among co-heirs. Recognized debt recalculated per expert quantification of actually incurred expenses within limitation exception raised. Loan lacking repayment deadline subject to court-set deadline per Art. 1817; deadline set at testator's death when will publication constituted actual payment request; limitation runs from succession opening. Co-heir debtor must attribute entire debt to estate per Art. 724(2), not pay directly to requesting co-heirs proportionally; applies equally to pretermitted heir admitted via successful reduction. Deceased's habitation right per Art. 540 over entire family-residence property (including co-heir's bare ownership portion) precludes compensation for non-enjoyment; lawful occupation by right-holder eliminates compensation basis. Exclusive use compensation requires co-owner expressed direct-use intent and denial; accrues only post-expression (October 2015 forward), not during habitation-right period. Maintenance contract validity requires alea—objective uncertainty at conclusion regarding: (a) annuitant life expectancy/care needs; (b) relationship between total annuitant-due benefits and transferred asset value. Alea exists when elderly but non-ill annuitant transfers modest-value property reserving usufruct with annuitant undertaking broad maintenance (beyond alimentary support) for two beneficiaries; bare ownership value (€145,638) reasonable for 12+ year estimated maintenance costs (€500/month × 2 persons). Annuitant financial self-sufficiency irrelevant; maintenance contract requires no need state unlike Art. 433 alimentary support. Original benefit disproportion proves simulation concealing donation; absent disproportion, no donation proven. Destination act per Art. 2645-ter valid as unilateral gratuitous transaction without ownership transfer (Cass. 3697/2020); settlor's allocation to satisfy stated needs (family member support/assistance) constitutes worthy-protection interests. Vehicle registration in deceased's name proves ownership via PRA entry; third-party payment irrelevant for ownership determination. Case remanded for expert estate formation based on rulings and division plan preparation considering defendant's expressed options.
